Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass: the excess exceeds 20% of optimal (4.2 km) and exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms. The route deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED on this trip's own measurement, and I rely on the governing trace figure rather than the rounded trip_record copy.

The driver admitted the detour in the in-app chat at 10:42:05 — 'sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now' — and repeated that admission in his own counterparty statement ('I took a wrong turn at the MCE exit and had to come back around'). A driver admission in the chat_log is itself an independent corroborating source named in POL-RD-07, and here it confirms the deviation without any need to lean on the trace alone.

ledger.claim: The chat log records no rider instruction to detour. The only rider messages are a question ('why we going towards city centre? MBS is the other side') and a bare 'ok'. No waypoint_hint is set on any message and no road is named, so the corroboration test for POL-RD-04 is not met and the clause is unavailable; the driver's own words attribute the detour to his missed exit, not to anything the rider asked for.

POL-RD-05 does not apply. Both pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null on the trip record and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so no endpoint was relocated and the booked optimal of 21.0 km stands as the baseline against which the excess is measured.

The rider has discharged the POL-RD-08 burden. Trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip TRP-00101, and the trace's first fix (10:21:05) matches the recorded start; the 6.18 km excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace (100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s, no jump over 500 m). The burden therefore shifts to the driver to invoke a specific exculpatory clause, and he has pointed to none — he has admitted the missed exit instead.

The rider carries no adverse claim pattern. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, far below the threshold of 4 in POL-RD-08, so the enhanced corroboration rule for low-substantiation riders does not apply and the claim is proven on the trace plus the driver's admission alone.

Under POL-RD-02 the refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. The fare model is METERED and recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 26.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63. The charged total is 35.64, so the refund is 35.64 - 27.63 = 8.01, rounded up to the nearest 0.05 as 8.05. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and is 22.5% of the charged total, well short of the 90% full-refund share, so the rider is owed a PARTIAL_REFUND of 8.05.

No off-route ERP or tolls complicate the correction: erp_gantries is empty and the ERP total is 0.00, so the entire difference sits in the distance and time charges that POL-RD-02 already corrects. There is no third-party pass-through line to net against the rider's refund.

Every artifact the rider's case rests on is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 — the trip record, the GPS trace, the chat log and the fare breakdown all carry no admissibility issues — so under POL-GEN-02 there is no impairment discount on the deciding facts, and the only zero-weight artifact is the advisory whose absence itself supports this claim.

The excess POL-RD-01 measures is 6.18 km over the 21.0 km optimal route, i.e. 29.43% (EV-GPS-00101 derived.deviation.excess_km / excess_pct). It clears the 20% establishment bar but falls short of both materiality thresholds in POL-RD-01 — 50% of optimal, or 8.0 km absolute. This deviation is therefore at most non-material, and the POL-RD-06 repeat-pattern machinery (the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) and the conduct referral in POL-RD-06(c)) is never engaged.

ledger.claim: For this METERED fare POL-RD-02 fixes the money arithmetically, not discretionarily: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 21.0 + 0.28 × 26.0) × 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63; refund = 35.64 − 27.63 = 8.01, rounded up to 8.05. The fare breakdown confirms these figures (recomputed_fare 27.63, refund.payable 8.05, refund_before_rounding 8.01). That 8.05 is the correct figure and the ceiling; the rider's contested 10.00 is not supported by the arithmetic.

The refund of 8.05 sits on a charged_total of 35.64, i.e. 22.47% of the charge (EV-FARE-00101 refund_share_of_charged). POL-RD-02 promotes a partial to a FULL_REFUND only where the refund reaches 90% or more of charged_total. At 22.47% that limb is nowhere near satisfied, so the only outcome the arithmetic can produce is a PARTIAL_REFUND — never the 35.64 full refund.

The fare carries no ERP or toll lines, no airport surcharge and no waiting-time fee (EV-FARE-00101: tolls_erp 0.00, erp_gantries empty, fixed_surcharges 0.0, waiting_time_fee 0.00). Under POL-RD-09(1) any off-route pass-through is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 recomputation and must never be added on top, and there is nothing here to add — the refund cannot be inflated beyond the arithmetic 8.05.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your route-deviation claim is upheld in part. The governing GPS trace measures the trip between the recorded pickup and dropoff at 27.18 km against a platform optimal of 21.0 km on the trip record — an excess of 6.18 km, or 29.43% of optimal. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km in absolute terms), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own measurement, and the driver's in-app message ('sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now') and his submitted statement both concede the missed MCE exit. It is not, however, a MATERIAL deviation (29.43% is under the 50% threshold and 6.18 km is under the 8.0 km threshold), so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check and any full-refund uplift do not arise. The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, not discretionary: charged_total 35.64 less recomputed_fare 27.63 — recomputed as (3.80 base + 0.75 x 21.0 km + 0.28 x 26.0 min) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee — gives a refund of 8.01, rounded up to 8.05. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and is 22.5% of the charge, well below the 90% full-refund share, so you receive a PARTIAL_REFUND of 8.05, not the 10.00 you asked for; your figure is not what the metered arithmetic produces. The fare carries no ERP, toll, airport surcharge or waiting-time lines, so there is no pass-through correction to add on top (POL-RD-09). To the driver: no exculpatory clause applies — there is no traffic advisory naming the corridor, no rider-requested detour in the chat log (no message carries a waypoint_hint and no road is named), and no pickup or dropoff amendment on the record — so the excess stands and the partial refund reflects only the distance and time overcharge. Your profile shows no repeat-deviation pattern (0 deviation_flags_90d over 812 completed trips, a ratio of 0.00), so no driver-conduct referral is made. Confidence is 0.95: every artifact the ruling rests on — the GPS trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown — is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02 cap is 1.0 and sits above the 0.70 platform floor.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
